name: How can I tell if my faucet needs a new washer, O-ring, or cartridge?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my faucet needs a new washer, O-ring, or cartridge?

acceptedAnswer.text: The type of faucet and where the drip originates often indicates the specific part needing replacement. For compression faucets, a drip from the spout usually means a worn washer, while a drip around the handle often points to a faulty O-ring. In cartridge, ceramic disc, or ball faucets, a continuous drip from the spout or base usually indicates a worn-out cartridge or disc assembly. Our plumbers can accurately diagnose the exact cause.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drip location and faucet type help identify the faulty part: spout drips often mean washers/cartridges, handle drips suggest O-rings. Professionals can confirm.
